newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian insurers profit rose in 1996 - association.
newsitem.headline: Belgian insurers profit rose in 1996 - association.

text.p: Belgian insurers will report a "slight improvement" in technical and financial results for 1996, Belgium's industry body, the Union of Professional Insurance Companies (UPEA/BVVO), said on Thursday.

"Commissions, as well as costs, will increase in line with premiums, while the rise in claims will be more limited, resulting in a slight improvement in the claims/premium income ratio," the UPEA/BVVO said in its 1996 annual report.
Capital gains on bond and equity portfolios meanwhile will compensate for the drop in dividend income on fixed-income holdings, it added.

The Union estimated that premium income on direct business rose 7.2 percent to 472.6 billion Belgian francs, from 440.9 billion francs in 1995, helped by continued strong growth in life insurance activities.

Premium income on life contracts rose 12.6 percent to 205.1 billion francs, with individual unit-linked life policy premium income jumping 255 percent to 5.5 billion francs. Income from interest-rate linked savings certificates, or bons d'assurance, in contrast fell 47 percent to 13.5 billion francs.
Non-life premium income rose 3.4 percent to 267.5 billion Belgian francs.
